body: Staff Review: Feature Envy. The Invoice class is too tightly coupled to the internal details of Customer and PricingPolicy. This is a classic example of 'Feature Envy' where a method seems more interested in a class other than the one it is in. We should move the logic to the classes that own the data.

comments.body: This method is exhibiting 'Feature Envy'. It is more interested in the Customer's membership level than its own state. This logic should be encapsulated within the Customer class.
Again, the Invoice is making decisions based on Customer's internal data. Consider moving this logic to a method in the Customer class, such as customer.isLoyal().
Feature Envy detected. The Invoice class is reaching into the Customer object to determine the discount. The Customer class should be responsible for calculating its own membership-based discount.
The logic for determining loyalty is leaked into the Invoice class. Move this to the Customer class to improve encapsulation.
